proposals: The Directorate General of Hydrocarbons should publish a CO₂-storage screening report from the National Data Repository, basin by basin, listing depleted fields and abandoned wells with the data available for storage study, so that named basins can be turned into named candidate sites.

The Petroleum Ministry should publish one national CO₂ storage-capacity estimate using a single method and reporting separately for hydrocarbon reservoirs, saline aquifers and coal seams, so that figures from 650 million to 270 billion tonnes are no longer quoted side by side.

Oil India should publish the five Assam depleted fields it shortlisted for storage and the stage reached in injectivity studies, so that its effort in the Barail and Tipam formations can be tracked beyond a February 2024 statement.

NTPC’s NETRA and IIT Bombay’s NCoE-CCU should publish the coalfield CO₂ Storage Atlas launched with NITI Aayog in November 2022, or a dated status note, so that a twelve-month commitment is accounted for.

ONGC should publish annual monitoring results from its Gandhar injection pilot — tonnes injected, reservoir pressure and leak checks, so that India’s first full-scale storage test produces public evidence on injectivity and containment.
